transcript.text: This is Swift, an automated flood assistant working with local emergency services. Am I speaking with someone at 1500 Afton Ridge Lane?
Yes, this is 1500 Afton Ridge Lane. I’m alone and the water’s not inside, but I can’t leave myself — I can help with a truck, not a boat.
Thanks for confirming your address and helping with a truck. How many people are at the home right now, including anyone who can't come to the phone?

There’s one person here, and I can help with a truck.  
*(corrects themselves)*  
Actually, there’s just me — no one else is here.

I hear you’re alone here — I’m here to listen. Is there anyone there who can't leave on their own, for example someone who uses a wheelchair, needs oxygen, or is bedbound? If it's a wheelchair, does it have a motor?
No, I’m alone and no one here can’t leave on their own. I just corrected myself — I’m the only person here.
Thanks for clarifying you’re the only person here. Is there water inside the home right now?
No, there’s no water inside the home right now. I’m the only person here, and I can help—there’s a truck available, but no boat or extra seats.
Thanks for your alert and readiness to assist. If neighbors need a ride out, do you have a high-clearance truck, a boat, or free seats in a vehicle?
I have a high-clearance truck available to help, but no boat or free seats in any vehicle.
Thanks for sharing your truck availability. Let me read that back: 1 people; no water inside yet; you can help with a truck. Is that right?
Yes, that’s right — one person here, no water inside yet, and I can help with a truck.

Thanks for confirming and offering the truck. I've recorded that you may be able to help neighbors. A dispatcher may contact you. Only go out if it's safe for you, and never drive into water you can't see the bottom of. Goodbye.
